title: Infrastructure for the Singularity — Jesse Han, Morph
talk_summary: Jesse Han of Morph pitches Infinibranch/Morph Cloud, a VM snapshot-and-branch substrate for agents, with demos of millisecond branching, parallel agent swarms racing against verifiers, and 'reasoning time branching'. The talk is mostly vision and product announcement; the only transferable mechanisms are snapshot/branch sandboxes, parallel best-of-N against verifiers, and idempotent durable agent workflows.

takeaways.what_they_do: Run agent VMs that can be snapshotted, branched, and rehydrated in milliseconds, so every action is reversible and parallel agents start from identical prepared state.
takeaways.evidence_quote: run entire virtual machines in the cloud that can be snapshotted, uh, branched and replicated in a fraction of a second
takeaways.numbers: branch in milliseconds rather than seconds

takeaways.what_they_do: Dispatch the same task to multiple parallel agents from one snapshot, each trying a different method, and keep the solution that passes a verification condition.
takeaways.evidence_quote: hand it off to as many parallel agents as you want and those agents will try different methods

takeaways.what_they_do: Agent steps are dispatched as idempotent, durable workflows chained on snapshots, so retries and re-runs don't duplicate side effects.
takeaways.evidence_quote: that will trigger an item potent durable agent workflow which is able to branch

takeaways.what_they_do: A parent agent decomposes a problem, delegates parts to subagents branched from an identical environment, then recombines results under a verification check.
takeaways.evidence_quote: the agent is responsible for delegating uh parts of its reasoning to sub aents which are branched off of an identical copy of the environment
